title: OA INITIATIVE MODIFIERS - the quickness doctrine with the character-only modifier clause, the tie rules and the printed kensai example
audit_comment: OA round sixty-eight (capture pp. 218-219): the Initiative Modifiers doctrine - the quickness frame, the character-only modifier clause with the phase division, the tie rules and the printed kensai example, single-pass pins per the Chapter 9 provenance shift

banner.title: OA INITIATIVE MODIFIERS, printed capture pp. 218-219 - the quickness doctrine round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture - the sole surviving pass per the R679 provenance shift. The doctrine frame: Oriental Adventures characters live and rely on their quickness and speed, some developing improved chances of striking the crucial first blow. THE CHARACTER-ONLY CLAUSE: when modifiers apply to only some of the characters involved, the initiative roll is still made only once for each side; those with modifiers apply their modifier to the die roll for their side BUT for the actions of that character only - the round may thus divide into more than two phases of attacks. THE TIE RULES: a tie (modified or unmodified) is not rerolled - all act in the same instant, and damage or spell effects are not applied to a same-initiative character until he has completed his action, the normal results then landing. THE PRINTED EXAMPLE: the 1st-level kensai, samurai and shukenja party rolls the 3, the hostile samurai the 4 - the kensai (modified 4) strikes in the same instant as the NPCs, then the remaining player characters; a hypothetical NPC kensai (modified 5) would strike first, then the simultaneous remaining NPCs and the PC kensai, then the survivors. THE LANDSLIDE RULE: when one side beats even the highest modified initiative of the other, the winning side completes all attacks in whatever order desired before the other side begins. The prose codifies per the R431 calculus

bools.name: diuOAQuicknessDoctrine
bools.comment: the doctrine frame - characters in the Oriental Adventures world live and rely on their quickness and speed, some having developed their speed to the point of improved chances of striking the crucial first blow (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOAInitiativeOncePerSide
bools.comment: the once-per-side rule - when modifiers to the initiative apply to only some of the characters involved, the initiative roll is still made only once for each side (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOAModifierCharacterOnly
bools.comment: the character-only clause - those characters with modifiers apply their modifier to the die roll for their side BUT for the actions of that character only (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOAPhasesExceedTwo
bools.comment: the phase division - thus the actions of an initiative round may be divided into more than two phases of attacks (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOATieNotRerolled
bools.comment: the tie rule - when the initiative (modified or unmodified) results in a tie, the die is not rerolled (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOATieSimultaneous
bools.comment: the tie simultaneity - all characters or creatures are assumed to be acting in the same instant (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOATieEffectsAfterAction
bools.comment: the tie resolution - damage done or the effects of spells are not applied to a character with the same initiative until he has completed his action; as soon as he has finished, he suffers the normal results of actions against him (print capture pp. 218-219)

bools.name: diuOAWinnerOrderUnimportant
bools.comment: the landslide rule - when the initiative of one side is greater than even the highest modified initiative of the other side, all characters on the winning side complete their attacks in whatever order is desired, their actions completed before those of the other side begin (print capture pp. 218-219)
